title: Integrating factors for nonexact equations
section: Nonexact Equations and Integrating Factors ▷ Factors depending on one variable
terms: nonexact equation; integrating factor; one-variable integrating factor; equivalent differen- tial equation.

exposition.text:
A nonvanishing function µ is an integrating factor when µM dx + µN dy is exact. Multiplication
preserves the equation only where µ is finite and nonzero. Thus singularities and zeros of a
proposed factor must be treated separately; an integrating factor need not exist globally on an
arbitrary region.

question.text:

Multiplying y − 1 = 0 by y gives y(y − 1) = 0. Which function solves the multiplied equation
but not the original one?
(A) y = x (B) y = x + 1 (C) y = x − 1 (D) y = 0 (E) y = 2x

solution.text:
The function y = 0 makes the multiplied equation zero identically, but its derivative is
zero rather than one. The first three functions solve both equations, while y = 2x fails the
multiplied equation except at one point. Multiplication by a factor that vanishes can add
solutions.

On x, y > 0, which is an integrating factor for dx + dy = 0?
x+y x+y
2
(A) x + y (B) 1/(x + y) (C) xy (D) (x + y) (E) 1/(xy)

solution.text:
Multiplication by x + y gives y dx + x dy = d(xy). This nonzero factor depends on both
variables. In fact the x-only criterion gives (x − y)/[x(x + y)] and the y-only criterion gives
(y − x)/[y(x+ y)], neither a function of the required single variable. Failure of those shortcuts
does not mean no integrating factor exists.
